Doggy day out programs near you

⁠‌​‌‍‌​‌‌​‌‌​‍​‌‍⁠A doggy day out (also called a dog day out, dog for a day, field trip or day trip) lets you check an adoptable dog out of a shelter for a few hours or a full day. You might go for a hike, grab a pup cup or just nap on the couch, and the photos and notes you share help the dog get adopted. It's almost always free.

Good to know

What is a doggy day out program?

A shelter program that lets the public borrow an adoptable dog for a few hours or a day. The shelter gives you a leash, an Adopt Me vest and often treats; you bring the dog back at the end of the outing.

Is there a doggy day out near me?

Search the programs below by state or city. If your local shelter isn't listed, look it up on our home page and send a request: we tell each shelter every month how many people asked.

How old do you have to be for a dog day out?

Usually 18 or older with a photo ID, and some shelters ask for a short orientation first. Each listing says what that shelter requires.

ShelterDayOut is a free directory. We don't run outings or handle bookings; each shelter sets its own rules. Listings are checked monthly, but details change, so confirm with the shelter before you go.

Ready to adopt? ShelterAdoption, our sister site, lists every shelter near you plus upcoming adoption events.
